chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf ibn Amira, from his father, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the sun declines, the time of Dhuhr enters, except that there is an optional prayer (subha) preceding it — and that is up to you: if you wish, prolong it, and if you wish, shorten it.

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The declining of the sun past its zenith (zawal), the astronomical marker for the start of Dhuhr time
key_terms.سُبْحَةً: Subha — the voluntary supererogatory prayers (nawafil) performed before the obligatory salat
key_terms.وَقْتُ الظُّهْرِ: The time of Dhuhr (noon obligatory prayer)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Dhuhr prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the Dhuhr prayer time begins at solar noon (zawal), while noting that there is a recommended supererogatory prayer (subha/nawafil) to be performed before the obligatory Dhuhr. The Imam leaves the length of this optional prayer to the discretion of the worshipper, affirming that it may be prolonged or shortened according to one's capacity and wish. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential understanding that nawafil before Dhuhr are recommended but voluntary in duration.
